page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with a few small marginal notes in the right margin. Below the text, the signature "F 2" at the foot. Running head at the top, page number "83" at the top right.

main_text.p: tum honesta ratio occurrat, aut ut liberos in armis exercendi occasionem nancisceantur, aut ut famam sibi & ad posteros memoriam e clade populorum emendicent. Et quis omnia humani cerebri portenta, in fraudem generis humani nata, recenseat? In statu po-pulari opifices, & id genus hominum, pacem lucelli causa morantur. Quod magis detestabile: belli civilis incendio domesticam ruinam nonnulli abscondunt. flagrantes inopia & cupidinibus, scelerum conscientia exagitati: quibus quies in seditionibus, in pace turbæ sunt: hi tumultum ex tumultu, bellum ex bello ferunt. S.H. lib.1. Hoc genus hominum, publico exitio na-tum, in solas insulas deportari, aut in primo ortu ex-tingui, illorum & reip. interesset.
main_text.head: Levi fermento ira offensi principis turgescens, longo vix tempore defervescit.
main_text.p: Quare non modo regnantes, sed & regnaturos aut offensa prius cultu officii devinci, aut offensa irritatos ne provocaoffensa prin-cipium re-crudescent.cipium re-. Tiberius Augusto regnante privatus, secreto recessu Rhodum coluerat. Archelaus Cappadociæ rex amicorum Romani nominis non in postremis, officii ab eo necessitudines averterat. quodnec Romani fastigii contemptu, ac ne quidem ignorantia Romani moris ab eo factitatum, in detrimentum ipsi vertit. quod sagaci pro temporum ratione consilio commisit, id imprudenter factum eventus evicit. Colere Tiberium paene exulem neglexerat, ab intimis Augusti monitis, quia florente C. Caesare, missoque ad res Orientis, intuta Tiberii amicitia credebatur. FactionibusEuripus aula. aula sæpè discinditur, aliis alium regni hæredem occulte aut palam destinantibus. nec ea semper ex affectu aut voto discessio: sed ut sibi quisque gratiam aut offensam fingit; imo ut fortuna velum, cum omni aura transfe-rendum, expandit. quæ res multos consilii prioris pœ-nitere, circumacta fortunæ aut favoris rota, cogiti

page.notes: The page number "83" is set in a stylised figure and may be read differently; marked with [?]. The running head is read as AULA TIBERIANA. Two marginal notes are the right-hand notes "offensa prin-cipium re-crudescent." and "Euripus aula."; their placement within the text follows the printed lines. A small reference mark appears beside "quod sa-gaci" in the right margin and is not transcribed. The sentence "quod sagaci pro temporum" and the word "factum" are read with some doubt. The last word "cogiti" is a fragment continuing on the next page.
